proposal.hypothesis: The seven distinct valid T2 programs measured so far are slower than the 0.001844 s baseline; the best reported two-target configuration, 96 threads, measured 0.002554 s. Test the contrasting smallest warp-aligned block: 32 threads map to 64 targets, yielding more one-warp CTAs while retaining two targets per thread and source-register reuse. This tests whether CTA granularity helps or whether one-warp blocks and reduced latency-hiding capacity outweigh that benefit; no speedup is assumed.

retained: Map each thread to targets blockIdx.x*(2*blockDim.x)+threadIdx.x and that target plus blockDim.x.
Load each source position and mass once per loop iteration, then reuse these values across two separate register accumulators.
Guard both targets independently for partial groups and write each valid target exactly once.
Use no shared-memory source tiling or block-level multi-output assignment.
